title: gateway guardrail routes: each endpoint-attached route has its own validator that reads its own request message
answers: Which permission check guards add, remove or update guardrail on a gateway endpoint?
Why does test_authorization_coverage fail after I change the guardrail routes?
How do I add a new route that modifies a gateway endpoint's guardrails?
body:
Path: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py guardrail validators for /api/3.0/mlflow/gateway/guardrails/add-to-endpoint, remove-from-endpoint, update-config and list-for-endpoint, which gate on the owning gateway endpoint's UPDATE or READ permission.
Rule: Each route maps to its own validator (validate_can_add_guardrail_to_gateway_endpoint, validate_can_remove_guardrail_from_gateway_endpoint, validate_can_update_gateway_endpoint_guardrail_config, validate_can_read_gateway_endpoint_guardrail_configs), and each parses its own protobuf request before calling _get_gateway_endpoint_permission. When adding such a route, register a route-specific validator and update the assertions in tests/server/auth/test_authorization_coverage.py that name the expected validator.
Symptom: Route-to-validator name assertions in test_authorization_coverage fail if the validator name is changed without updating the test.
Constraints: Applies to endpoint-attached guardrail routes; the generic validate_can_update_gateway_endpoint and validate_can_read_gateway_endpoint are used for the core endpoint routes, not these.
applies: Gateway guardrail endpoint routes and their authorization coverage tests.
says: Adding a guardrail to a gateway endpoint requires update permissions on that endpoint.
Users cannot remove or modify guardrails on endpoints they do not have access to.
Viewing guardrail configurations on a gateway endpoint fails when read access is missing.
Prevent unauthorized team members from modifying guardrail settings attached to an endpoint.
Updating an endpoint guardrail configuration requires edit rights on the parent endpoint.
search: Each endpoint-attached gateway guardrail route in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py must have its own dedicated validator that parses its specific protobuf request before checking permissions via _get_gateway_endpoint_permission. Routes for adding, removing, updating configuration, and listing guardrails (add-to-endpoint, remove-from-endpoint, update-config, list-for-endpoint) map respectively to validate_can_add_guardrail_to_gateway_endpoint, validate_can_remove_guardrail_from_gateway_endpoint, validate_can_update_gateway_endpoint_guardrail_config, and validate_can_read_gateway_endpoint_guardrail_configs to check the owning endpoint's UPDATE or READ permission. When adding a route, the route-specific validator must be registered and assertions in tests/server/auth/test_authorization_coverage.py:test_gateway_guardrail_gating must be updated to prevent route-to-validator test failures. This rule applies strictly to endpoint-attached guardrail routes rather than core endpoint routes, which use generic validators validate_can_update_gateway_endpoint and validate_can_read_gateway_endpoint.
